newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU stabilise - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU stabilise - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European monetary union, including Italy, Spain and Sweden, were higher this week, stabilising after a recent bout of EMU pessimism, according to JP Morgan's EMU calculator.
In the past five trading days, market prices indicated that the perceived probabilities of Spain, Sweden, Italy, the UK and Denmark joining Germany in EMU in 1999 all climbed higher.
The probability of Italy taking part rose 2.0 percentage points this week to 58 percent, Spain rose 3.0 points to 62 percent and Sweden rose 6.0 points to 66 percent.
Over the past month, EMU expectations registered a net decline only in Italy and Spain, which are down 5.0 points and 12.0 points respectively over that period.
Denmark, which rose 7.0 points this week, was also the biggest gainer over the month with a net 18.0 point rise to 55 percent.
Elsewhere, the perceived probability of the UK joining Germany in EMU in 1999 rose 4.0 points over the week but remains low overall with an estimated 39 percent chance.
The market still believes there is a 100 percent chance of France and Belgium joining in 1999, which was the same as last week, the calculator showed.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
